# Recipe — add a world object

**Use when:** the thing draws through a **`Renderer`** — `SpriteRenderer`, `ParticleSystem`,
`SpriteShapeRenderer`, `TilemapRenderer`, `MeshRenderer`. That is what makes it a world object.

**Ask the anchoring question first, and ask it per object (rule #16).** *What does this object
anchor to?* — a screen edge or the safe area (a HUD counter, a score readout, a top bar, a pill)
⇒ it belongs to the layer that owns it (`Ui` for screen furniture, `Popup` for dialog chrome,
`Overlay` for system overlays), and if it is uGUI this is the wrong recipe: route to
[`add-widget.md`](./add-widget.md). Only an object anchored to a position in the game's own space
reaches the draw-path question below. Answering once for a whole feature — "the board draws through
`SpriteRenderer`, **so** the score does too" — is exactly the failure this question exists to stop.

**The exception: a screen-anchored `Renderer`.** An edge particle burst or a full-bleed SpriteShape
backdrop is anchored to the screen but cannot be uGUI. `Stamp` it onto the owning layer and parent
it under that layer's host — a host canvas rides its camera every frame, which for screen-anchored
content is the behaviour you want. Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 below still apply; step 2 does not.

**The discriminator is how it draws, not whether it is "gameplay".** A uGUI graphic (`Image`,
`RawImage`, `TextMeshProUGUI` — anything on a `RectTransform`/`CanvasRenderer`) only renders as a
child of a `Canvas`, so it **must** go under a render-layer host canvas via `GetHost(id)` even when
it *is* the game: the shipped PingPong match view is uGUI throughout and is parented under
`GetHost(RenderLayers.GamePlay)`. If your gameplay view is built out of uGUI it is **not** a world
object — route to [`add-screen.md`](./add-screen.md) or [`add-widget.md`](./add-widget.md).

| The thing draws through… | It goes under | Recipe |
|---|---|---|
| a `Renderer` (`SpriteRenderer`, particles, tilemap, mesh) | the scene's `WorldRoot` | this one |
| a `Canvas` (`Image`, TMP, any `CanvasRenderer`) | `GetHost(id)` | [`add-screen.md`](./add-screen.md) · [`add-widget.md`](./add-widget.md) |

Both are `Stamp`ed. The measurement invariant this recipe applies is `architecture-map.md` §6; the
placement rig is §5.

## If it must receive taps — declare the mode, author nothing

**Decide this before you build the object.** World content reaches the EventSystem when **its layer
declares a physics raycast mode** in the layer manifest; the framework attaches the raycaster itself
at runtime. `GamePlay` already declares `"2d"`, so an object on the default gameplay layer needs **no
manifest change at all** — only the collider and the relay, points 3 and 4. A purely decorative
object declares nothing and pays nothing.

1. **Declare the mode on the layer** — one optional field on the manifest entry. This is how the
   framework's own `GamePlay` entry reads:

   ```json
   { "id": "GamePlay", "order": 0, "physicsRaycast": "2d" }
   ```

   > **A SKU almost never performs this step.** `framework.layers.json` ships inside the package and is
   > **read-only to a game**. The same field is legal in `Tools/Codegen/Manifests/game.layers.json`, but
   > **the rig binds only the six framework layers today** (`RootLifetimeScope` reads
   > `RenderLayers.WorldRaycastOf`, and it is `sealed`), so a mode declared on a *game* layer compiles
   > into `GameLayers.WorldRaycastOf` and then **reaches nothing, with no warning**. Until a rig seam for
   > game layers exists, put tappable world content on `GamePlay` — which already declares `"2d"`, so
   > you skip this step and step 2 entirely and go straight to the collider and the relay.

   The vocabulary is `"none"` | `"2d"` | `"3d"` and is **case-sensitive**: `"2D"` and `"physics2d"`
   are typos, not synonyms, and **fail codegen** with a message naming the layer and the legal set.
   Omitting the field means `none`. Declare it on the **one** layer that needs it — every camera
   carrying a raycaster pays a physics query per pointer event on the floor device, which is why the
   shipped framework manifest declares exactly one.
2. **Generate.**

   ```
   Framework/Codegen/Generate          (editor menu)
   # or: Tools/Build/pf-build.sh codegen
   ```

   The layer container gains `RenderLayers.WorldRaycastOf(id)` → `WorldRaycastMode`
   (`None`/`Physics2D`/`Physics3D`). **As the Root container is built** —
   synchronously, before any entry point and before the first scene loads —
   `WorldPointerRaycasterInitializer` hands the live rig to `WorldPointerRaycasters.EnsureOn`, which
   `AddComponent`s uGUI's `Physics2DRaycaster` (`2d`) or `PhysicsRaycaster` (`3d`) onto that layer's
   **camera**, get-else-add so it is idempotent. **Nothing is authored:** no prefab, no scene, no
   Inspector step, and the component is absent from every serialized scene (see **Gate**).

   Two properties are written on it, and both matter. `eventMask` is set to **that layer's own culling
   bit** rather than left open: the effective mask is `cullingMask & eventMask`, and the GamePlay camera
   is the one camera permitted to also mask Unity's built-in `Default`
   (`RenderLayerNaming.MayAlsoMaskDefault`, `m_Bits 513` in the shipped template) — left open, every
   `Collider2D` on `Default` would be tappable through it, including content never `Stamp`ed onto the
   layer. `maxRayIntersections` is set above zero because uGUI's default of `0` selects a raycast branch
   that **allocates a hit array on every pointer event**.
3. **Put a collider on the object** — `Collider2D` for `2d`, `Collider` for `3d`. It lives in the
   prefab, so it is human zone via Unity-MCP (rule #12). No collider, no hit.
4. **Relay from the View, in game units.** The View implements the uGUI `IPointer*` handlers and
   **relays**; the **controller** decides what the tap means. Rule #10 binds — convert to game units
   (a cell index, a reel index, a normalized axis) **before** emitting; for a physics raycast
   `PointerEventData.pointerCurrentRaycast.worldPosition` is already the world-space hit point, so
   no manual screen→world conversion is usually needed. Rule #9 still bans polling.
   `Assets/PingPong/Views/MatchSlice/MatchSliceView.cs` is the shipped relay shape
   (`IPointerDownHandler`/`IBeginDragHandler`/`IDragHandler` → a normalized axis).

**No `IPointer*` View base class ships, on purpose** — that would put `UnityEngine.EventSystems` on a
public framework API surface. Your View implements the handlers itself.

**Input priority is free and unchanged.** The EventSystem sorts camera-based raycasters by camera
depth, which *is* the rig's render band, so a dialog backdrop on `Popup` (20) and the
`IInteractionLock` blocker on `Overlay` (30) already beat world content on `GamePlay` (0). Blocking
order equals draw order, with no code on your side. **Across layers only, though:** within one
camera the comparer falls through to sorting layer, then sorting order, then hit distance — and this
raycaster shares the GamePlay camera with that layer's host-canvas `GraphicRaycaster`. A collider whose
GameObject carries no renderer reports sortingOrder 0 and competes with host-canvas UI on distance
alone, so do not rely on depth to separate world content from uGUI *on the same layer*.

## 1. Size it from the texture, never from `localScale`

The rig's ruler is **`1 texture px == 1 canvas reference px == 1 world unit`**. A 200×200 px sprite
imported at **PPU 1** is 200×200 world units — the same on-screen size as a 200×200 canvas `Image`,
at every aspect ratio.

- Import PPU is handled by `Assets/<Sku>/Editor/SpriteImportDefaults.cs` on an asset's **first**
  import. An asset that predates it keeps Unity's PPU 100 and warns on every re-import — fix it in
  the Inspector (`Pixels Per Unit = 1`). **Never** delete the `.meta` to re-trigger the default: that
  re-mints the GUID and breaks every prefab, scene and Addressables entry referencing the asset.
- **Two kinds of asset it silently never touches**, so check these by hand:
  - **`.psd` / `.psb`.** The postprocessor hooks `OnPreprocessTexture`, which only fires for a
    `TextureImporter`; a layered file goes through `PSDImporter` instead. It lands at **PPU 100 with
    no log and no warning** — the exact 100× error this step claims to prevent.
  - **Art outside `Assets/<Sku>/`.** The postprocessor's scope is that one folder; anything else
    returns before any inspection, and emits nothing.

  Same remedy for both: set `Pixels Per Unit = 1` in the Inspector — never by deleting the `.meta`.
- **Leave `localScale` at 1.** Scale is the animation channel (spawn pop, squash, punch). Sizing with
  it makes every tween fight the layout.
- Author inside `x ∈ [−540, 540]`, `y ∈ [−960, 960]` — the 1080×1920 design rect centred on the
  camera. That rect is visible on **every** device; a device off 9:16 adds bleed on one axis and
  never crops. Those are the numbers you *author* against. In **code**, inject `IWorldViewport` and
  read `SafeRect` instead of retyping them — and `HalfWidth`/`HalfHeight` when you need this device's
  real extent (bleed, off-screen spawn positions, clamping to the actual edge). Read per use; never
  cache a half-extent in a field.

## 2. Parent it under the scene's `WorldRoot`

Every screen scene ships a `WorldRoot` node — the screen template requires it
([`add-screen.md`](./add-screen.md) step 3). A `Renderer` needs no `Canvas` ancestor, so it goes
there:

```csharp
var worldRoot = gameObject.scene.GetRootGameObjects().First(g => g.name == "WorldRoot").transform;
var go = Object.Instantiate(prefab, worldRoot, false);   // false = worldPositionStays: false
```

`Object.Instantiate(prefab, parent)` is the `worldPositionStays: true` overload — with a non-identity
`WorldRoot` it back-computes the local transform to preserve world pose, which offsets the instance
**and rewrites `localScale`**, quietly breaking step 1's "leave `localScale` at 1". Pass `false`.

**Obtaining `worldRoot` is a rough edge.** There is no framework API — `ScreenBase` exposes only its
seven lifecycle methods and nothing is registered in DI, so the scene-name lookup above is the honest
current answer. It is a string match against a scene root, not an injected reference; treat it as
such.

**Why the parent matters here:** a render-layer host canvas is repositioned onto its camera's frustum
every frame by `WorldSpaceCanvasScaler`, so an object parented under a host **travels with the
camera**. `WorldRoot` is a plain scene node and stays where you put it. (A uGUI view has no choice —
it must be under the host canvas to render at all, and it accepts the camera-tracking as the point.)

## 3. `Stamp` it onto a render layer

```csharp
_layers.Stamp(go, RenderLayers.GamePlay, sortingOrder: 10);   // IRenderLayerRegistry
```

`Stamp` writes the Unity culling layer, the SortingLayer and `sortingOrder` down the **whole**
subtree, and forces `localPosition.z = 0` on every node in it. Skipping it leaves the object on its
prefab's layer — which on this rig does not always look broken (see **Common failures**).

## 4. Re-apply per-renderer `sortingOrder` **after** `Stamp`

`Stamp` writes **one uniform** `sortingOrder` to every `Canvas`/`Renderer` in the subtree, so any
in-prefab layering the artist authored is erased. If the object has internal order, set it after the
call:

```csharp
_layers.Stamp(go, RenderLayers.GamePlay, sortingOrder: 10);
shadow.sortingOrder = 9;    // after Stamp — before it, Stamp overwrites both
glow.sortingOrder   = 11;
```

Express in-object layering with `sortingOrder`, **never** with local z: `Stamp` zeroes z, and the
cameras are orthographic in a URP stack where stack order — not depth — decides which camera draws
on top (`architecture-map.md` §5).

## 5. Position in world units

The canvas plane is at `z = 0`; cameras sit at `z = −1000` with `near 0.3` / `far 2000`, so the
usable range is **`z ∈ [−999.7, +1000]`** — not symmetric, and anything outside it is **clipped**,
not just hidden. `Stamp` resets the stamped subtree's local z, so set z **after** stamping if you
need it at all. **Never read `Camera.orthographicSize`** to derive a size or a screen edge — it is owned by
`WorldSpaceCanvasScaler` and ranges ≈960–1200 by aspect. Call `IWorldViewport` instead:

```csharp
// injected: IWorldViewport _viewport   (tier-1 root singleton, no scene lookup)
var safe = _viewport.SafeRect;                                    // read once per use site, not into a field
go.transform.position = new Vector3(safe.center.x, safe.yMax - 100f, 0f);  // 100 units below the safe top
float spawnX = safe.center.x + _viewport.HalfWidth + 200f;                 // just off THIS device's right edge
```

**`HalfWidth`/`HalfHeight` are half-extents, not coordinates.** They are measured *from the camera
centre*, so a world x is `SafeRect.center.x ± HalfWidth` — using `HalfWidth` as an x only happens to
work while the camera sits at x = 0. `SafeRect` is the screen edge you are allowed to rely on
(identical on every device under `Expand`); the half-extents are this device's real extent. Both
recompute per read — read them where you use them, never into a cached field.

## Gate

```
Framework/Doctor        (editor menu)
```

Check 14 names a missing `SpriteImportDefaults.cs`; check 4 names a host canvas without its own
`GraphicRaycaster`. Then step the Game view through **1080×1920 · 1080×2400 · 1536×2048**: the object
must hold its on-screen size against a same-pixel canvas `Image`, and every host's `localScale` must
read exactly `1`.

**Verify world input with the boot smoke, never in the Inspector.** No editor check covers the physics
raycaster and none should: check 4 and `RenderRigBuildCheck` snapshot the *authored* scene outside
PlayMode, and the component is added as the Root container is built, so they cannot see it. Declaring
a layer's raycast mode is a **wiring** change, so it earns the one boot smoke §8a allows — boot once
(`pf-gates` has the procedure; the PlayMode *suite* is still CI's) and read the confirmation off the
console rather than by inspecting the live camera, which the smoke's sequence does not cover. The
`[WorldPointerRaycasters]` console line names the layer, the camera, and the single layer it raycasts.
It warns by name when two layers share one camera with different physics dimensions, and when the
declared type cannot be resolved. It does **not** warn for a layer whose camera slot is empty, because
that layer never reaches it — an unwired camera makes `GetHost`/`GetCamera` throw for that layer and
fails boot long before input matters.

> **A player build has one exposure no editor run can see.** The raycaster types are reached by name
> and referenced statically by nothing, so IL2CPP managed stripping would remove them and the attach
> would silently no-op in the APK. The package ships `Runtime/link.xml` to preserve them — if world
> input works in the Editor and not on device, that file is the first thing to check.

**Visual finish (rule #17).** Correct geometry is not a finished surface. A container that holds
slots draws its empty slots; the ground is a chosen colour, not the rig's `0.1, 0.1, 0.12`; gaps are
multiples of one spacing atom, not whatever made the grid fit the safe rect. Walk the eight-point
checklist in the `pf-visual-design` skill against the capture below.

Capturing evidence: pass an explicit **FHD size in the rig's own orientation** to `screenshot-camera`
(`width: 1080, height: 1920` on the shipped portrait rig; `1920×1080` if this SKU's design rect is
landscape). It defaults to landscape FHD and swaps that onto the camera, so on a portrait rig the scaler
recomputes for 16:9 and the capture shows ~3400 units of width — a picture of an aspect the game never
ships.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| A 100×100 px sprite is 1×1 unit, invisible next to the UI | It imported at Unity's default PPU 100 — it predates `SpriteImportDefaults`, carries a per-asset override, is a `.psd`/`.psb` (never seen by the postprocessor, and it logs nothing), or sits outside `Assets/<Sku>/`. Fix `Pixels Per Unit` in the Inspector; do **not** delete the `.meta`. |
| The object drifts with the camera instead of staying in the world | It is parented under a `GetHost(...)` host canvas. Hosts are repositioned onto their camera every frame. Reparent under `WorldRoot`. |
| A score/HUD readout is right at 9:16 but wrong on a tall phone and ignores the notch | It is under `WorldRoot` because the feature around it draws through `Renderer`s — the draw path was answered once for the whole feature. Anchoring is decided **per object** (rule #16): a readout anchored to a screen edge is a uGUI widget under `GetHost(RenderLayers.Ui)` — that host is the `SafeArea` child, so the notch inset is free and a `GraphicRaycaster` reaches it with no collider — no matter how the rest of the feature draws. Route to [`add-widget.md`](./add-widget.md). |
| The object has a collider but receives no `IPointer*` callback | One of the four links is missing. Its layer declares no `physicsRaycast` (only `GamePlay` ships `"2d"`) · the manifest was edited but codegen never ran · the collider is the wrong dimension for the declared mode (`Collider` under `"2d"`) · the object was never `Stamp`ed, so it is not on the declaring layer's culling layer and `camera.cullingMask` excludes it. Read the `[WorldPointerRaycasters]` console lines first — they say whether the raycaster was attached and to which camera. |
| Correct at 9:16, wrong on a tall phone | A hardcoded `960` / `orthographicSize`, or a size derived from `Screen.*`. `orthographicSize` is scaler-owned and aspect-dependent; use world units and read `IWorldViewport` — `SafeRect` for the guaranteed rect, `HalfWidth`/`HalfHeight` for this device's real extent. |
| Layering inside the object collapsed after placement | `Stamp` wrote one `sortingOrder` to every renderer in the subtree. Re-apply the per-renderer values **after** the call. |
| An authored z offset vanished | `Stamp` forces `localPosition.z = 0` on the whole subtree. Set z after stamping, or express the order with `sortingOrder`. |
| It was never `Stamp`ed, and it is either invisible **or** visible-but-mis-ordered | **Rig-dependent, so do not diagnose from the symptom.** Read the `GamePlayCamera` culling mask in your Master scene: masking its own layer alone ⇒ un-`Stamp`ed content renders on no camera (invisible); *also* masking the built-in `Default` (permitted, not required) ⇒ it draws at the GamePlay band but keeps its prefab's SortingLayer, so its ordering against `Stamp`ed siblings is wrong. Either way: check `gameObject.layer` and call `Stamp`. |
| A 9-sliced `Image` or `SetNativeSize()` blew up 100× | `Canvas.referencePixelsPerUnit` is not 1. It is written at runtime by `WorldSpaceCanvasScaler` and never serialized, so a canvas without that component loads at Unity's default 100. |
